# Josh & Jordan's Kitchen

> No-talking home cooking and scratch baking from Josh & Jordan's Kitchen. Josh cooks savory meals by feel with no measuring cups; Jordan runs the oven. Tight method cuts, minimally cut full-process sessions, kitchen tools, and recipes.

Josh & Jordan's Kitchen is published by Built by Josh Studio LLC (https://builtbyjoshstudio.com/llms.txt). Contact: support@builtbyjoshstudio.com.

## About & Authority

- **Josh & Jordan's Kitchen** is a home cooking and baking channel on YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/@joshandjordanskitchen) and this site: no-talking home cooking and scratch baking, filmed two ways — a tight method cut, or a minimally cut full-process session at normal speed.
- **Josh Tran** cooks the savory side, and the Vietnamese classics, by feel with no measuring cups. He learned by watching his dad cook most nights, and wrote Nước Mắm — A Vietnamese Family Cookbook (https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/cookbook/). He also builds the free kitchen tools on this site.
- **Jordan** bakes: the breads, sweets, and pastries come out of Jordan's oven. Josh cooks, Jordan bakes.
- **The free kitchen calculators** (https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/) are free and ad-free with no signup. They run entirely in your browser: nothing you type is uploaded or collected.

## Cookbook: Nước Mắm — A Vietnamese Family Cookbook

Page: https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/cookbook/ · Author: Josh Tran · Publisher: Built by Josh Studio

My family's recipes, written down at last — the Vietnamese food I grew up eating, taught the way my dad taught me: salty, sweet, garlic, heat, balanced by tasting, not measuring. The ratios are starting points, doorways, never destinations: the recipe is your first attempt; your tongue does the rest.

Formats and prices:
- Ebook, direct: EPUB + PDF in one zip, 56 pages, 7 chapters, instant download — $3.99 (https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/cookbook/)
- Kindle edition: $3.99 on Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HBCXTLWD)
- Etsy edition: $3.99 on Etsy (https://www.etsy.com/listing/4551851115/nc-mm-vietnamese-family-cookbook-o)
- Paperback: $7.99 on Amazon, 80 pages, ISBN 979-8188988173 (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HBL7HZYN)

Chapters:
1. Nước Mắm — the sauces that run the whole book, starting with the fish sauce my dad made at the same counter where he taught me to cook.
2. Summer Rolls (Gỏi Cuốn) — fresh rolls the way we make them at home, and the rolling technique that stops them falling apart.
3. Bún Bowls — rice-noodle bowls built to balance: herbs, protein, pickles, and the dressing that ties it together.
4. Over Rice — the weeknight backbone: the dishes my family actually eats over a pot of rice.
5. Fried Spring Rolls (Chả Giò) — the crispy ones, including which shortcuts are worth it and which aren't.
6. Bánh Mì, My Way — store-bought bread, homemade everything else.
7. Phở — the twelve-hour one.

Also in the book: an introduction about learning to cook at my dad's counter; the Shopping Guide (what to buy and what it's called at the store); taste-as-you-go ratios; the honest shortcuts (store-bought buns, rotisserie chicken); which recipes are my dad's, and which quietly became mine.

## Phở: the twelve-hour simmer and the two-day method

These are two methods, not conflicting numbers. Nước Mắm includes both: Dad's traditional twelve-hour phở simmer, and Josh's two-day broth-on-broth method. The two-day method is also written up on the blog (https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-make-pho-two-day-method/): an eight-hour beef broth on day one, then about five hours of phở simmer on day two with the stored bones from day one, plus a one-day version for when you don't have two days.

## Kitchen tools

- [Air Fryer Conversion Calculator | Oven to Air Fryer, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/air-fryer-conversion-calculator/): Convert any oven recipe to air fryer settings — temperature, time, and when to check, tuned by food type. Fahrenheit or Celsius. Free, ad-free, no signup.
  - Rule: lower the oven temperature by about 25°F (15°C) and cut the time by about 20%, then adjust by food type — frozen foods and cut vegetables run faster, large roasts and baked goods want gentler heat and more of their original time.
  - First check at roughly two-thirds of the converted time; cook in a single layer. Example: 400°F for 30 minutes becomes 375°F for about 24 minutes, first check at 16 minutes.
  - Confirm meat and fish by thermometer: 165°F poultry (ground poultry included), 160°F burgers, meatballs and sausage, 145°F fish, 145°F plus a 3-minute rest for steaks, chops and roasts of beef, pork, veal and lamb.
- [Brine Calculator | Free Wet & Dry Brine Salt & Time Math](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/brine-calculator/): Calculate wet or dry brines for turkey, chicken, pork, and more. Get precise salt amounts, water ratios, sugar options, and brining time recommendations.
  - Wet brine: 0.6 L of water per lb of meat (2 L minimum), salt at 5% of the water (4% light, 6% strong) — 50 g of salt per liter. Equilibrium brine: salt at 1.5% of the meat and water combined. Dry brine: salt at 1% of the meat's weight (0.75% light, 1.25% strong), about 4.5 g per lb.
  - Salt by volume varies: coarse flaky kosher salt is about 8 g per tablespoon, table salt about 18 g, so weigh it. Example: a 12-lb turkey takes about 7.2 L of water and 360 g of salt in a standard wet brine.
  - Times: wet brine about 1 hour per lb for whole birds, chicken pieces and roasts (never under 30 minutes; chicken capped at 4 hours, turkey, duck and goose at 24 hours); steaks and chops 30 minutes to 1 hour; fish and seafood 15 to 30 minutes; ground meat isn't wet brined. Dry brine 1 to 2 hours per lb (at least 1 hour; poultry capped at 24 hours). Equilibrium brine at least the standard time, up to 2 days. Don't brine "enhanced" meat.
- [Cookware & Pan Guide | Free Kitchen Utility](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/cookware-pan-guide/): Select the best cookware material and pan shape for any cooking task. Interactive advisor, material explorer, and care guidelines. Free, ad-free, local-first.
  - Stainless steel and enameled cast iron are non-reactive and safe for acidic foods; long acid contact strips the seasoning on bare cast iron and carbon steel.
  - Induction needs a magnetic base: cast iron is magnetic, stainless only if a magnetic alloy (430 stainless) is clad on the bottom — a fridge magnet should stick firmly. Skip aerosol cooking sprays on nonstick; their residue ruins the release.
  - Matching: stainless builds fond for pan sauces, seasoned carbon steel suits high-heat stir-frying, cast iron stores heat but responds slowly, copper responds almost instantly.
- [Cost Per Serving Calculator | Free Recipe Cost Calculator](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/cost-per-serving-calculator/): Free cost per serving calculator. Enter what you used, the pack size, and the pack price to get total recipe cost and price per serving. No signup, no ads.
  - Ingredient cost = pack price × (amount used ÷ pack size). Cost per serving = total ingredient cost ÷ number of servings. A waste allowance adds a buffer for trim and spoilage; most kitchens use 5% to 15%.
  - Example: spaghetti with meat sauce for four costs $12.24, or $3.06 a serving (example prices); with a 10% waste allowance, $13.46 or $3.37 a serving.
  - Pricing rule of thumb: ingredients at roughly 28% to 35% of the menu price — at 30%, a $3.06 plate prices at $10.20. Labor, packaging and overhead are not included.
- [Bread & Dough Hydration Calculator | Pizza & Pasta, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/dough-hydration-calculator/): Bread hydration calculator for bread, pizza, and pasta dough. Enter your flour and get water, salt, and yeast by baker's percentage. Free, no ads, no signup.
  - Hydration % = water weight ÷ flour weight × 100; flour is always 100%. Flour = target dough weight × 100 ÷ (100 + hydration % + salt % + yeast %).
  - Presets, salt 2% of flour (leavened doughs add yeast at 1%): Tokyo ramen 35%, soba 40%, egg pasta (semolina) 45%, Neapolitan pizza 60%, French baguette 65%, sourdough boule 72%, Italian ciabatta 82%.
  - Limits: all-purpose turns slack much past 65%; pasta warns past about 48%; egg pasta swaps the water for whole eggs at about 50 g each. Example: 1,000 g of sourdough dough at 72% is 571 g flour, 411 g water, 11 g salt, 6 g yeast.
- [Turkey & Meat Thawing Time Calculator | Fridge or Cold Water](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/meat-thawing-planner/): How long to thaw a turkey, chicken, roast, or steaks: enter the weight and get safe fridge and cold-water thawing times from USDA guidance. Free, no ads.
  - Refrigerator: about 24 hours per 5 lb (whole turkey about 4 lb per day), with minimums of a full day for poultry, roasts, game and ground meat and 12 hours for steaks, chops and fish. Turkey: 12 lb 3 days, 16 lb 4 days, 20 lb 5 days.
  - Cold water: about 30 minutes per lb (turkey about 36), in a leak-proof bag, fully submerged, water changed every 30 minutes; past 6 hours the calculator recommends the refrigerator instead. Cook cold-water-thawed meat right away; fridge-thawed meat keeps another day or two.
  - Danger zone 40°F to 140°F: never thaw on the counter. Open vacuum-sealed fish and seafood before thawing. Source: USDA's Big Thaw guidance.
- [Baking Pan Conversion Calculator | Swap Cake Pan Sizes, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/pan-swap-calculator/): Swap one baking pan for another: round, square, rectangular, muffin, or Bundt. Get the ingredient multiplier and a bake-time warning. Free and ad-free.
  - Multiplier = new pan volume ÷ original pan volume, where volume is footprint × depth (round: π × radius²). A 12-cup muffin tin counts as 6 cups brim-full and a Bundt as 10 cups, both raised 13% to compare like with like.
  - Examples: 8-inch round to 9-inch round at the same depth takes 1.27 times the batter; a 9x5 loaf recipe scales to about 1.7x for a 9x13 (2 inches deep), not the 2.6x its footprint suggests.
  - Moving to a much deeper pan: lower the oven about 25°F and add 15 to 20 minutes, checking the center with a toothpick.
- [Perfect Roast Pull Temp Calculator | Carryover Cooking Math](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/perfect-roast-pull-temp-calculator/): Calculate the exact temperature to pull your roast, steak, or turkey from the oven to account for carryover cooking. A free, ad-free culinary utility.
  - Carryover cooking raises the internal temperature 2°F to 15°F after the meat leaves the heat: a thin cut at moderate heat 2–3°F, a large roast at high heat 10–15°F.
  - Examples: a large beef roast at 350°F aiming for medium-rare (135°F) pulls at 128°F; a medium-rare steak pulls roughly 3–6°F early.
  - Safe finals are enforced: 145°F pork and fish, 160°F ground meat, 165°F poultry; 140°F to reheat a fully cooked ham.
- [Recipe Nutrition Calculator | Calories & Macros Per Serving](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/recipe-nutrition-calculator/): Paste a recipe's ingredients and get calories, protein, carbs, and fat per serving, plus an estimated Nutrition Facts label. Free, no ads, no signup.
  - Per-serving nutrition = each ingredient's calories and macros for the amount used, summed, ÷ servings. Calorie split uses 4-4-9: 4 kcal per gram of protein, 4 per gram of carbohydrate, 9 per gram of fat.
  - Say dry or cooked: 100 g of dry jasmine rice becomes roughly 250 g cooked. Example: pancakes for four come to 335 calories a serving (35 from protein, 183 from carbohydrate, 115 from fat).
  - Estimates for home cooks; not compliant with FDA labeling regulations.
- [Roast Cooking Timeline Calculator | Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/reverse-roasting-calculator/): Work backward from serving time to plan your roast — covering turkey, chicken, beef, pork, lamb, and ham with rest and prep buffers.
  - Works backward from serving time: subtract the rest, then the roasting time (minutes per lb × weight), then prep; it also allows for preheat and the oven's recovery when cold meat goes in.
  - Pork profiles (USDA roasting chart): loin about 20 min per lb at 350°F; shoulder (Boston butt) about 45 min per lb at 350°F; ham about 20 min per lb at 325°F. Loin and ham rest 10 minutes under 2 lb, 20 minutes up to 8 lb, 40 minutes above; a shoulder holds 1 hour in an insulated cooler, a brisket 2 hours.
  - Example: a 6-lb shoulder is about four and a half hours in the oven plus the 1-hour hold, so a 6 p.m. dinner means the oven goes on at noon. Whole pork cuts: 145°F (63°C) minimum with a 3-minute rest; ground pork 160°F.
- [Universal Recipe Scaler | Ad-Free Ingredient Converter](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/universal-recipe-scaler/): Instantly scale, multiply, or divide cooking and baking recipes. A free, local-first utility to convert portions and metric measurements with zero ads.
  - Multiply every quantity by the same factor; it converts between metric and US units as it scales. Salt, strong spices, garlic and leavening don't scale linearly — scale them, then taste toward the lower end. Cooking times change with volume, but not proportionally.
  - Example: meatloaf for four at 2x — 1½ lb ground beef becomes 3 lb, ⅓ cup milk becomes ⅔ cup, 2 eggs become 4, and the oven stays at 350°F.
- [Yeast Converter | Active Dry, Instant, & Fresh Yeast Ratios](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/yeast-converter/): Convert yeast measurements between Active Dry, Instant, and Fresh yeast. Convert grams, ounces, teaspoons, and packets with automatic weight guards. Free, ad-free.
  - By weight, active dry : instant : fresh is about 1 : 0.8 : 2.4 — instant is about four-fifths the weight of active dry (active dry about 1.25 times instant), and fresh about 2.4 times active dry or about 3 times instant.
  - Example: one 7 g packet of active dry equals 5.6 g instant or 16.8 g fresh; a 7 g packet of instant is about 21 g fresh. Fresh yeast is measured by weight only, never by teaspoon.

## Blog posts

- [The Baking Pan Swap Calculator — Free Pan Conversion Tool](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/baking-pan-swap-calculator/): Convert any recipe between pan sizes — square, round, rectangle, muffin tin, Bundt — with an instant scaling multiplier and bake-time warning. Free, no signup.
  - The short version: When a bake goes sideways between pan sizes, the recipe is rarely the problem — the pan geometry is. This is a free, ad-free, local-first utility: pick the pan a recipe calls for, pick the pan you actually own, and get the exact ingredient multiplier in one click. It covers cake-to-muffin-tin and Bundt conversions without doing 3D volume math by hand, plus a bake-time warning when the swap changes batter depth.
- [Building the Brine Calculator: Brining Math Worth Getting Right](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/brine-calculator/): Build notes on the brine calculator: why brining math matters, what it handles — salt type, protein weight, brine strength, time — and how it fits the kit.
  - The short version: Brine ratios aren't one-size-fits-all: salt density varies wildly by type, so a tablespoon of flaky kosher salt carries far less actual salt than a tablespoon of table salt. A wet brine submerges the meat in a salt-water solution; a dry brine rubs salt on the surface and lets it reabsorb overnight. The free Brine Calculator does the salt-density and weight math for you — wet or dry, four salt types, optional sugar, with a brining-time recommendation and a built-in timer.
- [Building the Universal Recipe Scaler — Local-First, Ad-Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/building-the-universal-recipe-scaler/): How I built a free, instant recipe scaler — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no backend, localStorage, JSON-LD — the regex problem, scale-lock logic, and a clean, fast interface with an interactive prep checklist.
  - The short version: A frustration-driven side project: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, browser localStorage, no backend, no ads, no signup. Scales ingredient quantities and converts US imperial to metric. The regex problem nobody mentions, the scale-lock logic that ignores temperatures, and a clean, fast interface with an interactive prep checklist.
- [Cook the Way You Want to Cook — Against Culinary Purism](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/cook-the-way-you-want-to-cook/): A daily home cook's argument for cooking the way you want to cook. The only rules worth following are food safety and a few real technique rules. Everything else is yours.
  - The short version: Unless you own a restaurant, cook the way you want to cook. The only rules worth following are food safety and the small set of techniques that are actually physical laws (you can't make a roux without flour and fat). Everything else is opinion.
- [How to Calculate Cost Per Serving (Formula + Examples)](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/cost-per-serving-calculator/): The cost per serving formula with worked examples: package price to per-serving math, waste allowances, and the mistakes that throw the number off.
  - The short version: The cost per serving of a dish is its total ingredient cost — the cost of the amounts you actually used, plus a small waste allowance — divided by the number of servings. The fiddly part is converting package prices into the cost of the portion you actually used, and the one rule that quietly breaks the math is comparing a weight against a volume. This guide walks the whole method by hand, step by step, so the number means something — the free Cost Per Serving Calculator just automates it once you understand it.
- [Dough Hydration Calculator — Baker's Percentages](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/dough-hydration-calculator/): Free baker's-percentage calculator for bread, pizza, pasta, and noodle dough — flour absorbency warnings, egg conversion for fresh pasta, kansui math for ramen.
  - The short version: A free baker's-percentage calculator for bread, pizza, pasta, and noodle doughs. Flour is locked at 100% and everything else scales as a percentage of that flour weight, with two calculation modes (target total dough weight or target flour mass), eleven flour types across five flour groups, six traditional style presets (Neapolitan, sourdough, baguette, ciabatta, Tokyo ramen, soba), and built-in checks for flour absorbency limits, unleavened noodle doughs, kansui salts for ramen, and whole-egg conversions for fresh pasta.
- [How I Actually Cook Rice — The Finger Method, No Measuring Cup](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-cook-rice-finger-method/): The Vietnamese finger method for rice-cooker water, from someone who has cooked rice a few thousand times. Jasmine rice, rice cooker, no measuring cup required.
  - The short version: Jasmine rice in a rice cooker, rinsed until the water mostly clears, water added by knuckle — small batch uses pinky, larger batch uses index finger. Twenty-five years of finger-measured rice and zero failures I couldn't blame on my own distraction.
- [How I Learned to Cook — From Watching My Dad to Tuesday Gỏi Cuốn](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-learned-to-cook/): Watching my dad cook most nights, the first dish I made alone at twelve, and why I still cook gỏi cuốn on weeknights — on learning to cook by absorbing it.
  - The short version: On growing up in a Vietnamese-American kitchen, the first thing I cooked alone, why I make gỏi cuốn on weeknights and phở when it matters — and the recipe scaler I built for everyone who learned cooking a different way.
- [How I Make Phở at Home — The Two-Day Method (and Spinach)](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-make-pho-two-day-method/): A home cook's two-day, stock-first phở bò — every step explained, honest non-traditional choices included (spinach in the bowl), plus a one-day shortcut.
  - The short version: A two-day phở bò method: roast a shin bone, beef knuckle, and oxtail instead of par-boiling (saving the rendered fat as beef tallow), build a rich beef broth on day one for eight hours, and store the bones overnight. On day two, pull those stored bones back out and simmer them in the day-one broth for about five hours, with a spice sachet in the last couple of hours. Use roughly two tablespoons of fish sauce while it cooks — keep it light in the pot and adjust to taste in the bowl. Sautéed garlicky spinach goes at the bottom of the bowl. Squid brand fish sauce. A one-day version is included for when two isn't possible.

  - The short version: Active dry, instant, and fresh yeast are the same organism carrying different amounts of water, so they aren't interchangeable gram-for-gram — instant is the most concentrated, fresh the least.
